t: The second paragraph of section 2421 of title 18, United States Code, is amended by striking out, after “such person to”, the word “induct,”, and inserting in lieu thereof the word “induce,”.

fable.w: This section is a purely technical amendment that corrects a typographical error in 18 U.S.C. 2421, replacing "induct" with "induce". There is no tempting participation reading: it involves no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section is a purely textual amendment to a criminal statute, changing the verb from 'induct' to 'induce'. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, advisory boards, or hearings. It merely defines the scope of a criminal prohibition.

opus.w: This provision only replaces the word "induct" with "induce" in section 2421 of title 18, which is a clerical correction. It does not provide for consultation with outside parties, public comment, hearings, advisory bodies, rulemaking, or a right to sue. Amending a statute does not by itself bring anyone outside the federal government into a federal decision.
